entries.title: OpenAI Fires Three Safety Researchers Who Warned Company Could Lose Ability to Monitor AI Chain-of-Thought
entries.summary: OpenAI fired researchers Tomek Korbak, Jasmine Wang, and Mikita Balesni for alleged 'breach of trust'; the trio publicly accused the company of prioritizing corporate interests over safety and urged the board in a letter to preserve chain-of-thought monitoring capability and collaborate with independent safety auditors — the most serious public safety-culture rupture at the company since prior high-profile departures.

entries.title: Nadella: Treat Every AI Model as Already Compromised — Containment Must Sit Outside the Model
entries.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella publicly argued that organizations should never trust an AI model as a clean system, calling for containment frameworks covering tamper-proof audit logs, independent audits, timely incident disclosure, and the ability for authorized staff to pause or shut down a model mid-task — directly shaping enterprise AI risk governance expectations.

entries.title: Senate Bill S.5576: Frontier Developers Would Owe New Federal AI Safety Board Pre-Release Model Access Plus Mandatory Incident Reporting
entries.summary: S.5576, sponsored by Senators Warner, Schatz, and Kim, would require frontier AI developers to give a new federal AI Safety Board access to each model including its weights at least 45 days before public release, and would establish mandatory incident reporting and a public AI incident database.

entries.title: TRACE: Renaming Agent Tools Drops Evaluation Scores by 0.25 With Zero Behavioral Change — Verifier Brittleness Is the Hidden Audit Variable
entries.summary: TRACE is a controlled diagnosis protocol showing that agent evaluation systems are brittle — renaming tools lowers a scripted agent's score by 0.250 even when the agent performs identical operations, and identical reruns flip 15–36% of task outcomes, exposing a deep gap between measured scores and actual capability that undermines AI auditing.

entries.title: Risk Ceilings and Development Deadlines Cannot Both Be Guaranteed When AI Safety Productivity Is Unknown
entries.summary: An economic model shows that a regulator can simultaneously promise a maximum risk ceiling and a development deadline only if weak safety research can be ruled out in advance, with a calibration showing a 3.3% safety-productivity margin needed above the necessary bound — a foundational constraint for AI governance frameworks.

entries.title: NeuroSploit: Structured Multi-LLM Pentest Harness Achieves 96–100% Active Directory Technique Coverage, Full Compromise in 134 Minutes
entries.summary: A benchmark of nine frontier LLMs inside a structured multi-agent harness achieves 96–100% Active Directory technique coverage with 90–97% precision — versus 21–54% for direct LLM invocation — demonstrating how close current AI agents are to fully autonomous enterprise cyberattack capability when properly orchestrated.

entries.title: Cited but Not Consulted: LLMs Name Legal Authorities Correctly but Verdict Rarely Changes When That Authority Is Swapped
entries.summary: A counterfactual audit across seven open-weight models finds that while models name the correct legal authority in 66.7–100% of generations, the verdict changes when the authority is substituted in only 0–76.7% of cases, making named legal authority a poor proxy for genuine compliance grounding and undermining LLM-generated legal explanations as audit artifacts.

entries.title: Correct Verdicts, Flawed Reasoning: ~60% of Accurate LLM Vulnerability Analyses Contain Fabricated Claims, Evading LLM-as-Judge
entries.summary: VERA, an automated structured-reasoning-record auditing framework, finds that approximately 60% of correct vulnerability verdicts from LLMs include fabricated or unverifiable reasoning claims, and that free-form chain-of-thought allows these errors to evade LLM-as-judge evaluation — VERA exposes 87% of reasoning errors that standard judges miss.

entries.title: Same Outcome, Different Evidence: Pairing Attack Success Rate With 'Operative Understanding Rate' Reveals Hidden LLM Safety Failures
entries.summary: Proposes pairing ASR with an 'operative understanding rate' that measures whether a model actually engaged with the evaluated harmful task, showing that identical low-ASR values can correspond to very different underlying safety postures — models may simply fail to parse an attack rather than genuinely resist it.

entries.title: EviLLM: Supply-Chain Adversaries Can Inject Vulnerabilities From 13 CWE Classes Into LLM-Generated Code via a Compromised Account
entries.summary: EviLLM demonstrates a realistic threat model in which a third-party adversary with access only to a compromised account or browser silently injects software vulnerabilities from 13 CWE classes during LLM-assisted code generation, with 7/8 and 10/13 user study participants failing to detect the injected flaws.

entries.title: OnTrack: ~1ms-per-Step Streaming Agent Monitor Correctly Aborts 83% of Failing Runs, Saving 18% of Wasted Compute
entries.summary: OnTrack compares a live agent trajectory against historical successful runs in approximately one millisecond per step, enabling real-time intervention before irreversible actions are taken, and aborts 5 of 6 cases that were genuinely heading to failure — a practical, low-latency approach to the hard problem of continuous agent oversight.

entries.title: GWU Develops Mathematical Formula to Predict On-Device AI Chatbot Safety Failures Before They Occur
entries.summary: George Washington University researchers validated a formula that predicts when AI chatbots will produce unsafe or undesirable outputs across seven open-weight models, and propose an in-model early-warning system — directly relevant to deployed AI that operates without cloud-based safety filters or live monitoring.

entries.title: Cooldown Landmines: Two Attacks Let a Tenant Force Another Tenant's LLM Gateway Requests to Fail
entries.summary: Two attacks in LiteLLM exploit shared cooldown records so that one tenant can redirect another tenant's traffic to inferior fallback deployments with zero upstream calls — demonstrating fundamental tenant isolation failures in shared LLM infrastructure that remain even after quota enforcement.
